entities.summary:
Hywel ap Ieuaf was a pivotal figure in the history of Gwynedd, King of North West Wales from 979 to 985. His reign marked a crucial period of political instability and power struggles within the kingdom. The succession crisis triggered by his death led to the eventual unification of Gwynedd under a single ruler.

As a key player in Welsh politics during the medieval era, Hywel ap Ieuaf played a significant role in shaping the region's future. His leadership was marked by controversy and power struggles with rival claimants to the throne.

Despite his tumultuous reign, Hywel ap Ieuaf left a lasting legacy in Gwynedd, paving the way for its eventual integration into the Kingdom of Wales under later rulers.
